About Bitdeer:

Bitdeer is a world-leading technology company for AI and Bitcoin mining infrastructure. Bitdeer is committed to providing comprehensive Bitcoin mining solutions for its customers and building AI computational infrastructure to support the AI revolution. Bitdeer handles complex processes involved in computing such as equipment procurement, transport logistics, data center design and construction, equipment management, and daily operations. Bitdeer also offers advanced cloud capabilities to customers with high demand for artificial intelligence.

Headquartered in Singapore, Bitdeer has deployed data centers across multiple countries, including the United States, Norway, Bhutan, and Ethiopia. To learn more, visit https://ir.bitdeer.com

We are seeking

Bitdeer is seeking a Senior Commercial Contracts Manager to join our Legal & Compliance team in San Jose, CA. This individual will primarily focus on commercial contract operations — intake, execution discipline, recordkeeping, and obligation tracking — across Bitdeer’s North America construction, procurement, and site development activity. This is an operational and process-discipline role, not an attorney position.

What you will be responsible for

  • Serve as the single point of intake for commercial contracts across the North America function — vendor and supplier agreements, purchase orders, NDAs, membership-program paper, and routine amendments — and route each to the appropriate business and legal owner.
  • Build and own a central, searchable repository of executed agreements, capturing contract type, counterparty, effective and expiry dates, value, signatory, and status.
  • Administer the signature and execution workflow, confirming authorized signatories and a complete, correctly executed signature page before work begins or payment is released, and escalating exceptions immediately rather than after the fact.
  • Maintain a tracking calendar for renewal and auto-renewal windows, notice-to-terminate deadlines, insurance certificate expirations, and milestone and performance dates, and surface them to the responsible deal owner with enough lead time to act.
  • Own first-pass review and negotiation of standard agreement types against Bitdeer’s negotiation playbook and pre-approved fallback positions, escalating any requested deviation to the assigned attorney.
  • Evaluate and help implement a contract lifecycle management platform, and maintain the reporting that measures contract volume by type and business unit, cycle time, and workload.
  • Support the Legal & Compliance team on other contract operations matters as assigned.

How you will stand out

  • 8+ years in contracts management, contract administration, or legal operations. A law degree is not required for this role and is not a substitute for the experience described above.
  • Demonstrated experience building or substantially improving a contract intake, tracking, or repository process from a low-maturity starting point — this is a build, not a maintain-the-existing-system role.
  • Working fluency with a contract lifecycle management or e-signature platform (DocuSign, Ironclad, ContractPodAi, or equivalent), including comfort evaluating and selecting tools rather than only using them.
  • Strong, demonstrated process discipline and organizational rigor, with the judgment to operate within a playbook and escalation framework rather than deciding legal positions independently.
  • Excellent communication skills, with a collaborative mindset and high self-motivation.
  • Experience in a construction or EPC, energy, industrial procurement, or hardware and technology environment with high-volume deal flow.
  • Prior experience at a public company, with the recordkeeping and disclosure rigor that implies.
  • Experience supporting multi-entity, multi-jurisdiction operations across the United States and Canada.

Bitdeer is committed to providing equal employment opportunities in accordance with country, state, and local laws. Bitdeer does not discriminate against employees or applicants based on conditions such as race, color, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, marital and/or parental status, religion, political opinion, nationality, ethnic background or social origin, social status, disability, age, indigenous status, and union.
descriptions.job-0fb9kez:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Corporate Security Systems and Infrastructure (CSI) team safeguards Stripe’s people, offices, and operations by designing, delivering, and maintaining secure infrastructure across our global workplace portfolio. We take an intelligence-led, risk-based approach and partner closely with Workplace, IT, Security Operations, Legal, and external vendors to build reliable, scalable physical security systems and transition them to our Global Security Operations Center (GSOC) for ongoing monitoring and support.

What you’ll do

As a Corporate Security Infrastructure Project Manager, you will lead the security infrastructure workstream for new offices, expansions, relocations, and major workplace upgrades, with an initial focus on Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) and support for global projects as needed. You will manage projects from early site assessment and design through installation, testing, commissioning, and operational handover.

You will be accountable for scope, schedule, budget, risk, quality, and stakeholder alignment across a portfolio of concurrent projects. In addition to delivering individual projects, you will strengthen the CSI program by improving standards, documentation, vendor performance, reporting, and repeatable project management processes. You will work through ambiguity, surface decisions early, and communicate clearly with technical teams, business partners, vendors, and senior leaders.

Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end delivery of security infrastructure for office construction and expansion projects, from site assessment and requirements definition through design, procurement, installation, testing, commissioning, and closeout.
  • Lead requests for proposals (RFPs) for security installations, including defining scope and requirements, coordinating bidders, reviewing submissions, evaluating proposals with relevant stakeholders, and supporting vendor selection recommendations.
  • Own project scope, schedule, budget, risks, dependencies, decisions, and change control; provide clear, outcome-focused reporting to stakeholders and leadership.
  • Coordinate security designs and technical requirements with Workplace, IT, Security Operations, Legal, architects, general contractors, landlords, and other project partners.
  • Review design drawings, specifications, bills of materials, and implementation plans to ensure alignment with CSI standards and local requirements.
  • Manage security integrators, consultants, and contractors, including statements of work, delivery milestones, quality expectations, service levels, and performance reviews.
  • Oversee system installation, acceptance testing, commissioning, punch-list resolution, documentation, and first-day-of-business readiness.
  • Ensure completed projects are smoothly handed over to the GSOC and support teams, with accurate system records, operating procedures, training, and ownership established.
  • Maintain and improve global construction standards, technical specifications, project templates, runbooks, and closeout documentation.
  • Develop and track project health metrics, vendor KPIs, budget forecasts, and lessons learned; use insights to improve delivery quality, predictability, and cost efficiency.
  • Support new market and site evaluations by identifying security risks, infrastructure constraints, integration needs, and mitigation options.
  • Support the security repair and maintenance program, with a focus on the EMEA region, collaborating with regional teams to triage, track, and resolve security system and hardware issues.
  • Partner with CSI engineers and program leadership to prioritize work, resolve cross-project dependencies, and scale consistent processes across the portfolio.
  • Travel up to 25%, including international travel, to support site assessments, project milestones, commissioning, and handover.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of project management experience delivering complex physical security, workplace technology, low-voltage, construction, or similarly technical infrastructure projects.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple concurrent projects across the full lifecycle, with ownership of scope, schedule, budget, risk, quality, and stakeholder communication.
  • Experience coordinating cross-functional delivery among technical teams, business partners, design and construction teams, vendors, and senior leaders.
  • Strong vendor and contractor management skills, including defining requirements, managing contracts or statements of work, tracking delivery, and addressing performance issues.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate technical details into clear decisions, risks, tradeoffs, and next steps for different audiences.
  • Strong judgment and structured problem-solving skills; able to operate independently, navigate ambiguity, anticipate issues, and drive timely decisions.
  • Meticulous attention to detail and a demonstrated commitment to accurate documentation, standards, and operational handoffs.
  • Experience establishing project management processes, tracking performance metrics, and applying lessons learned to improve future delivery.
  • Working knowledge of physical security systems such as access control, video management, intrusion detection, intercoms, low-voltage infrastructure, and door hardware.
  • Ability to travel internationally up to 25%.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience delivering security infrastructure for offices in multiple countries or regions, particularly in EMEA.
  • Experience with Genetec Security Center, including Synergis, Omnicast, Security Center SaaS, or Stratocast; active Genetec certification is a plus.
  • Familiarity with system integrations, networking fundamentals, APIs, webhooks, or cloud-managed security technologies.
  • Experience managing budgets, forecasts, vendor KPIs, SLAs, and portfolio-level reporting.
  • Experience using project management and workflow tools such as Jira and Smartsheet.
  • Experience reviewing and marking up construction and security design documentation using Bluebeam Revu or a similar PDF design-review tool, along with knowledge of commissioning practices and relevant local codes or regulatory requirements.
  • A bachelor’s degree in project management, construction management, security management, information technology, engineering, or a related field; or a relevant professional certification such as PMP, PRINCE2, ASIS PSP/CPP, or SIA CSPM.
  • Ability to select and use appropriate AI tools to improve work, while critically evaluating and refining outputs for accuracy and quality.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by technology. Founded in 2017, we are revolutionising world systems through our cutting-edge digital asset exchange, Web3 portal and blockchain ecosystems. We reshape the financial ecosystem by offering some of the most diverse and sophisticated products, solutions, and trading tools on the market. Trusted by more than 50 million users in 180 countries globally, OKX empowers every individual to explore the world of Web3. With our extensive range of products and services, and unwavering commitment to security and reliability, we provide an essential trading platform for the world's investors and institutions. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. As strong believers in the value of blockchain technology, we are committed to building a more inclusive and open financial future and we know that starts with the people who build it.
 

About the team

OKX's Global Legal team provides legal advice and guidance to OKX and its affiliated entities across all coverage areas and geographic locations, and supports business growth by working with all teams within the company to help them achieve their goals. We are a high-functioning, collaborative and fast-paced team who enjoys the cutting-edge nature of our work and our industry. Our team of 60+ lawyers are located around the world, and the OKX Chief Legal Officer is based in the United States.
 

About the opportunity

As Deputy General Counsel and Head of Legal, UK, you will lead the UK legal function, working closely with the UK CEO and other key UK stakeholders and reporting into the Global Legal team. You will provide strategic legal advice to the UK business and work closely with global legal colleagues and senior business leaders on regulatory, commercial and strategic matters.
 
You will be a member of the UK management team and represent the legal function at relevant Board and committee meetings.
 
The right candidate will have direct legal experience and an enthusiastic belief in the digital asset space, 14+ years of experience working for a top-tier law firm, in-house at a financial services or digital assets company or with a financial services regulator and possess excellent writing and analytical skills. The ideal candidate has deep experience in financial services and digital asset regulation, U.K. licensing, marketing and advertising, and contract law.
 
We offer a competitive base salary and bonus structure as well as excellent benefits and an opportunity to work in a cutting-edge industry that will be the future of financial services.
 

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Supporting OKX's business expansion into the United Kingdom. This role will be the primary legal point of contact for the OKX U.K. entity, and will be called upon to support the business in its licensing and legal efforts to expand into the U.K. Market. The right candidate will also have experience in government and regulatory relations and will be responsible for ensuring OKX is a valued contributor to the developing legal frameworks in the sector. This will include representing OKX in relevant industry associations and promoting OKX's view point in consultation efforts.
  • Supporting the business in virtually all legal coverage areas, including but not limited to product development, regulatory matters, IP and trademark enforcement, corporate governance, licensing efforts, token listings for OKX U.K., contract negotiation, compliance legal support, institutional sales and partnerships, and marketing and advertising;
  • Analyzing and advising on the legal risk of new and existing digital assets and managing the legal component of the new asset review process;
  • Collaborating with product and business development teams to achieve company-wide projects and goals; and
  • Managing legal requests from all areas of the business and effectively advising on legal concepts and legal risk with an eye towards the strategic goals of business leaders.
  • You will be working from OKX's London office three days a week. You may work remotely two days a week.

What We Look For In You

  • Law degree at a top-tier law school and qualified to practice law in the U.K.
  • 14+ years of legal experience at a top-tier law firm and/or in-house legal team, preferably in the cryptocurrency/digital assets and/or financial services industry.
  • Experience advising on digital asset and blockchain technology legal issues and have a basic understanding of the relevant legal and regulatory landscape.
  • Experience working with the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and obtaining U.K. financial services and/or crypto exchange licenses.
  • Comfortable working independently in a fast-paced, growth-stage and multi-cultural environment.
  • Ability to effectively advise and build trust with business teams.
  • Ability to navigate through a rapidly-changing legal landscape and deal with legal ambiguity.
  • Ability to work in a high-functioning legal team and feel comfortable in a collaborative working environment.
  • Self-starter, quick learner who is highly driven, proactive, responsive and precise.
  • Experience working on cross-jurisdictional matters and a global legal team.

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company events
  • Wellness and meal allowances 
  • Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependents 
  • More that we love to tell you along the process!

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

 

We're looking for a Sr. Data Analyst, Compliance to join our team remotely! The primary goal of this role is to elevate decision-making by uncovering emerging trends and root causes, and by driving insights and actions that provide full visibility into business performance and operational efficiency.

Beyond technical expertise, success in this role depends on being a true business partner who combines data-driven insights with strategic thinking to deliver actionable recommendations, guide decision-making, and drive measurable impact across the organization.

In this role, you'll own end-to-end data management, from building and maintaining datasets and pipelines to designing dashboards and delivering insights for the Compliance team. A core part of this role is owning the logic and rule-setting behind transaction monitoring across deposits and withdrawals. You'll also contribute to experimentation infrastructure, laying the groundwork for future ML and intelligence initiatives.

 

The opportunity

  • Own the logic and rule-setting behind transaction monitoring across deposits and withdrawals, partnering closely with Compliance to study patterns and refine detection logic

  • Translate compliance requirements into production detection logic, preserving correctness across alert eligibility, thresholds, customer segmentation, date windows, and deduplication

  • Develop and maintain Python and SQL pipelines for transaction data preparation, feature engineering, and detection workflows

  • Evaluate detection rules and analytical models across coverage, alert quality, threshold sensitivity, and the impact of proposed changes

  • Design reproducible evaluations on historical data that account for limited labels, class imbalance, and shifts in customer behaviour over time

  • Own testing, deployment, scheduling, monitoring, and operational support for detection workflows, including investigating data quality issues, pipeline failures, and unexpected changes in detection results

  • Execute historical backfills with clear validation and traceability, and maintain reliable downstream alert delivery and integrations with compliance systems

  • Be at the forefront of data innovation by experimenting, testing hypotheses, and translating insights into action, while incorporating software engineering best practices into pipelines and dashboards.

 

What you bring

  • 7+ years of experience in data analysis, data science, and data management within the fintech, crypto, financial services, or gambling industry, gained in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

  • Experience working with compliance, fraud, funding, finance, and customer support teams and analyzing large datasets, engineering features, and applying statistical methods to practical business problems

  • Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience building and supporting production data or analytical systems

  • Hands-on experience using dbt or similar tooling to model and organize high-fidelity data for reporting and decision-making

  • Experience setting up and managing data pipelines with a strong understanding of workflow orchestration, plus strong software engineering practices including version control, automated testing, code review, and CI/CD

  • Solid statistical foundation; ML exposure is a strong plus

  • Proficiency with BI and data visualization tools (e.g., Hex, Tableau, Power BI, or similar) to build executive-facing dashboards

  • Ability to investigate production issues independently and communicate technical findings and uncertainty to non-technical stakeholders

  • You believe wholeheartedly in the values outlined in Kraken's Tentaclements document

  • A degree in a field emphasizing analytical rigor, such as analytics, software engineering, statistics, or economics

  • Based in Canada, the US, or Brazil, and fluent in English

 

Nice to haves

  • Fraud detection, AML, anomaly detection, or other risk applications

  • Experience with Athena, Trino, Kafka, and Kubernetes alongside the core Airflow/dbt/S3 stack

  • Transaction pattern analysis, customer segmentation, and detection threshold tuning

  • Developing or productionising machine learning models, including experiment tracking and performance monitoring

  • Working with sparse or delayed feedback from investigations to evaluate and improve detection

  • Explainability, auditability, and change control in regulated environments

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.

We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.

As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

About us

BVNK is the stablecoin-powered financial stack for enterprises. We're now part of Mastercard, and together we're building a network for every form of money – one that delivers more reach, more capability and more choice.

We enable businesses to build financial products, unlock new markets, and move money in seconds across 130+ countries, with 40+ licenses for fiat and digital assets globally. Processing billions annually, we empower enterprises worldwide to send, receive, convert, and settle stablecoins and fiat seamlessly through a single integration.

Our mission is to accelerate global money movement, and we're assembling a world-class team to make it happen.

Trusted by industry leaders like Corpay, Worldpay, Deel, and Flywire, we deliver the infrastructure that makes new forms of money usable within the financial systems customers already rely on today.

By combining Mastercard's global payment reach and trusted networks with BVNK's stablecoin infrastructure, we're building the trusted operating layer for the evolution of money movement, helping customers participate in emerging digital networks without having to rebuild their businesses around every new innovation.

We're a diverse team spread across EMEA, North America, and APAC, with a shared belief that stablecoins are the new infrastructure layer for financial services, and that BVNK is at the forefront of this shift.

We're incredibly honored to have been recognized by:

  • CNBC World's Top Fintech Companies (2026)

About The Role:

As a Solutions Engineer at BVNK, you will be a technical partner to our commercial teams and prospective customers throughout the sales process. You will lead the technical strategy for some of BVNK’s most complex and strategic opportunities, helping customers understand how BVNK’s products and infrastructure can support their business and technical requirements.

You will sit at the intersection of Sales, Product, Engineering, Compliance, and Delivery, combining deep technical expertise with strong commercial judgment and executive-level customer communication.   • Act as the technical owner for strategic, complex, and enterprise customer opportunities throughout the sales process.
  • Partner closely with Sales and Account Management to develop technical strategy, qualify opportunities, and progress deals toward successful close.
  • Lead complex technical discovery across customer architecture, payment flows, integration requirements, regulatory considerations, operational processes, and business objectives.

  • Provide market, competitive, and customer insights back into BVNK to help shape product strategy, commercial strategy, and roadmap priorities.

What we need from you:

  • Strong understanding of payments infrastructure, payment flows, and financial technology ecosystems.

  • Demonstrated ability to design and communicate complex end-to-end technical solutions across multiple systems, products, and stakeholders.
  • Experience owning technically complex enterprise sales opportunities from discovery through technical validation and close.
  • Ability to identify technical risks, dependencies, and product gaps early while remaining pragmatic and solutions-oriented.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage credibly with software engineers, architects, product leaders, security teams, compliance stakeholders, and senior executives.
  • Strong commercial judgment and a clear understanding of how technical decisions influence sales cycles, deal progression, implementation success, and long-term customer outcomes.
  • Experience leading technical workshops, architecture discussions, product demonstrations, and executive-level customer conversations.
  • Ability to manage multiple complex and high-priority opportunities simultaneously.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills across Sales, Product, Engineering, Compliance, Security, and Delivery.
  • Experience mentoring or providing technical leadership to other Solutions Engineers is highly desirable.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, evolving environment with a high degree of ownership and autonomy.
  • A proactive mindset, strong judgment, and a bias toward solving complex customer problems in a scalable way.

We Offer:

  • Flexible working hours, with remote working at its heart.
  • A flexible approach to holidays. 
  • Opportunities to travel to our offices around the world.

At BVNK, we are focused on building a diverse and inclusive team. While you may not meet all of our requirements, we’d encourage you to apply if you meet the majority of our expectations. You may be a great fit for this role or another role in our team.

Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role:

We're seeking a Senior Brokerage Operations Associate (Canada). An experienced individual contributor who has lived dealer, clearing, and custody reality and designs every process as if manual work is temporary.

You turn CIRO-aligned operating requirements into scalable, automated, auditable workflows that Product and Engineering can build against. You partner closely with the ACCC President / UDP, Compliance, Product, Engineering, and global Ops. Someone who influences through expertise, crisp documentation, and decision logs, not through a team.

Success is measured by launch readiness, STP and control quality, registered-account / tax operability, and systems others can run and not by headcount or heroic spreadsheet ops.

What you'll walk into:

You won't be starting from zero. You'll be owning live problems:

  • Getting ready to open: figure out how we open and maintain accounts, process trades, and hold client cash and securities on day one. Build that for ACCC rather than copying a manual process from another firm.
  • Working with partner brokers: define how a partner firm and ACCC split the work on accounts, trades, and holding client assets, so it still works as volume grows.
  • After the trade: settlement in Canada (through CDS), trades that fail to settle, and corporate actions such as dividends and splits. Automate the routine cases and keep a clear list of exceptions, instead of running the book in spreadsheets.
  • Registered accounts and tax: TFSA, RRSP, RESP, and similar accounts. Cover who can open them, contribution rules, what a security cost, tax withheld on dividends and other income, and the reports clients and partners need.
  • The day after launch: written steps for daily work, checks that our records match the custodian and the market, contacts at vendors and custodians, and a plan if a system or vendor fails. Have these ready before real client volume shows up.
  • Building Canada: clear handoffs between product, engineering, and operations teams.

What you’ll own:

  • Account lifecycle & client/introducing-broker servicing (onboarding handoffs, KYC/AML ops interfaces, maintenance, transfers)
  • Trade lifecycle (capture, affirmation, clearing, settlement, fails, breaks)
  • Custody & asset servicing (segregation, security movements, corporate actions, cash)
  • Books & records, reconciliations, exception management, and operational controls
  • Registered accounts & tax ops: TFSA, RRSP, RESP and related wrappers; tax lots / cost basis; withholding; local reporting partners need to stay compliant
  • Day-2 production ops: runbooks, escalations, vendor/custody interfaces, BCP/DR operational playbooks

How you’ll work:

  • Translate Canadian reality into runnable process — CIRO-aligned dealer/clearing/custody expectations, introducing–carrying dynamics, custody controls, and operational risk into SOPs, RACI, controls, and exception paths Product and Engineering can build against
  • Automation-first by default — redesign high-volume / high-risk / high-friction work for straight-through processing, rules, exception queues, and measurable SLAs, instead of spreadsheet heroics
  • AI-first operating lens — Prototype and productize AI-assisted ops (exception triage, recon investigation, SOP Q&A, control-testing support, runbook copilots) with human oversight where risk or regulation requires it
  • Go-live and beyond — Readiness for ACCC launch and early production; continuous improvement after go-live
  • Raise the bar without managing a team — Coach partners through expertise, crisp documentation, and decision logs; leave systems others can run

How we'll measure success:

  • Launch readiness gates met with documented controls, SOPs, RACI, and runbooks Product / Eng / Ops can execute against
  • STP, exception, and reconciliation aging targets defined and trending the right way post go-live
  • Registered-account and tax workflows ready when partners launch, rather than added later
  • Specs and decision logs that remove re-discovery for Product and Engineering
  • Systems and playbooks others can run after you, so knowledge sticks in the org and not only in one person's head

Who you are (Must-haves):

  • 10+ years deep, hands-on Canadian brokerage operations experience at a CIRO dealer, carrying broker, custodian, clearing firm, or brokerage ops function in Canada

When something goes wrong for a customer and the normal path hasn't fixed it, the case lands with you. You'll own how Polymarket handles escalations and formal complaints end to end: intake, classification, resolution, root cause analysis, and reporting. The scope covers trust, safety, and community concerns alongside standard customer disputes, and it has to meet regulatory and audit expectations. Documentation discipline matters as much as resolution speed here.

This is a build role. Polymarket's CX function is growing, and a formal escalations and complaints program doesn't fully exist yet. You'll define what gets escalated, how, and to whom, set service levels, and make sure every case file is clean enough to hand to a regulator. You'll work closely with Legal, Compliance, Trust and Safety, Product, and Engineering, which means you need to be as comfortable writing a case summary for outside counsel as you are talking a frustrated customer off a ledge.

  • Maintain complete, accurate case records and produce reporting that Legal, Compliance, and external auditors can rely on.
  • Train front-line agents and AI systems on escalation criteria, handoff procedures, and documentation standards so the program works at scale.

  • 4 or more years in escalations, complaints management, or customer resolution at a fintech, bank, brokerage, or other regulated company.
  • Direct experience building or running a formal complaints program, including intake design, case tracking, and regulatory reporting.
  • Strong written communication skills, particularly in sensitive situations where tone and precision both matter.
  • Rigorous documentation habits and a clear understanding of what "audit-ready" actually means in practice.
  • Sound judgment and a consistent sense of fairness when cases are ambiguous or emotionally charged.
  • Comfort working directly with Legal and Compliance teams, including translating case details into formats they can act on.
  • (Plus) Experience handling regulator-referred or formal consumer complaints, such as CFPB or state-level filings.
  • (Plus) Background in Trust and Safety or community moderation, especially in a platform or marketplace context.

Benefits

Pay Transparency
